summary: Austria has now answered this in writing, and the answer is unusually clear. The health ministry (BMASGPK) ruled on 3 August 2026 that the roof rat is NOT a domesticated animal, so it is not a pet species in law. Rodents count as Heimtiere under TSchG 4 Z 3 only if they are domesticated; because the ministry holds R. rattus is not, it falls into the residual category of Wildtier under 4 Z 4. That single classification drives everything else. You may keep one, but only after filing a notification (Anzeige) with your district authority (Bezirksverwaltungsbehoerde) under TSchG 25 together with 8 Abs. 1 Z 1 of the 2nd Animal Husbandry Ordinance, within two weeks of starting. Breeding needs no second filing: TSch-SV 34 says a separate breeding report under TSchG 31b Abs. 1 is unnecessary if it was included in that same Anzeige. A real permit is only triggered above 300 juveniles given away per year (TSchG 31b Abs. 2 Z 4, permit under 23), which is far beyond a hobby colony. Housing must meet point 3.8 of Anlage 1 of the 2. THVO. So: legal, one form, no permit at hobby scale. A second letter from the same ministry, dated 23 September 2026, settles what breeding involves beyond that filing. Since 19 June 2026 the 7. Abschnitt of the Tierschutz-Sonderhaltungsverordnung (TSch-SV) applies to anyone keeping roof rats for breeding, whether the breeding needs only a Meldung or a full Bewilligung, because the section's only exemption covers domesticated Haus- und Heimtiere. The breeder must keep written or electronic records on the breeding animals and hold them for at least five years after each animal's litter date, ready for inspection. From 1 January 2027 an information leaflet must go with every animal handed over, and the ministry says this applies to animals given away free as well as sold. The ministry adds that binding interpretation of these rules belongs to the provincial (Bundesland) authority.
agency_confirmations: Bundesministerium fuer Arbeit, Soziales, Gesundheit, Pflege und Konsumentenschutz (BMASGPK), Sektion III, Gruppe B/Abteilung 16 (veterinary law), written and officially signed reply of 3 August 2026 (Geschaeftszahl 2026-0.635.895-2-A; amtssigniert 2026-08-03), answering our inquiry of 24 June 2026: (1) rodents are Heimtiere under TSchG 4 Z 3 only if domesticated, and in the ministry's view the roof rat is not domesticated, so it is a Wildtier under 4 Z 4; (2) as a wild animal it may be kept only on an Anzeige to the locally competent Bezirksverwaltungsbehoerde under TSchG 25 with 8 Abs. 1 Z 1 of the 2. THVO, exemptions at 25 Abs. 2; (3) breeding otherwise needs a Meldung under 31b Abs. 1, but TSch-SV 34 waives a separate one where it was made within the 25 Anzeige; (4) a Bewilligung under 31b Abs. 2 Z 4 is required only above 300 juveniles given away per year; (5) rat housing follows point 3.8 of Anlage 1 of the 2. THVO. The letter does NOT address transfer of the notification duty to a new keeper, sell/give generally, or transport and import.

Bundesministerium fuer Arbeit, Soziales, Gesundheit, Pflege und Konsumentenschutz (BMASGPK), Sektion III, Gruppe B/Abteilung 16, written and officially signed reply of 23 September 2026 (Geschaeftszahl 2026-0.792.715; amtssigniert 24 September 2026), answering our follow-up of 18 August 2026: (1) because the roof rat is a Wildtier under TSchG 4 Z 4, the exemption in TSch-SV 33 Abs. 1 Z 1 and 2 does not apply, so the 7. Abschnitt of the TSch-SV governs keeping roof rats for breeding; (2) it applies whether or not the breeding needs a Bewilligung under TSchG 31b, so also where only the 31b Abs. 1 Meldung applies; (3) the breeder keeps the records listed in TSch-SV 28 Abs. 1 Z 1 to 7, on paper or electronically, for at least five years after the litter date of the animal concerned, open to inspection at any time (28 Abs. 2); (4) the information duty of TSch-SV 29 applies also when an animal is given away free of charge; (5) binding interpretation of the TSchG and its ordinances rests with the locally competent Bundesland.

keep.why: Legal, on a notification. The BMASGPK confirmed in writing (Geschaeftszahl 2026-0.635.895, 3 August 2026) that R. rattus is not domesticated and is therefore a Wildtier under TSchG 4 Z 4, not a Heimtier under 4 Z 3. Wild animals with special husbandry needs may be kept only on the basis of an Anzeige to the district authority, to be filed within two weeks of starting and again within 14 days of stopping (TSchG 25 Abs. 1, with 8 Abs. 1 Z 1 of the 2. THVO). Exemptions from that duty are listed in TSchG 25 Abs. 2. The Anzeige carries the keeper's name and address, the species and maximum number of animals, and the place of keeping. Housing must meet point 3.8 of Anlage 1 of the 2. THVO. Nothing here is a permit: it is a filing, and the ministry did not attach any approval condition to keeping.
keep.governing_law: TSchG (BGBl. I 118/2004) 4 Z 3 and Z 4 (Heimtier vs Wildtier), 25 Abs. 1 and Abs. 2 (Anzeige, two weeks); 2. THVO (BGBl. II 486/2004) 8 Abs. 1 Z 1, Anlage 1 point 3.8 (rat housing); BMASGPK written ruling 2026-0.635.895 of 3 August 2026.

breed.why: Legal, and it needs no second form. Breeding normally triggers its own report to the district authority under TSchG 31b Abs. 1. For wild animals the Tierschutz-Sonderhaltungsverordnung 34 removes that: a separate 31b Abs. 1 Meldung is not required where the report was already made within the TSchG 25 Anzeige. So one filing, made once and covering breeding, is the whole obligation. That provision entered force on 19 June 2026, which is why our earlier research did not have it. A genuine permit (Bewilligung under TSchG 23) is required only above the 31b Abs. 2 Z 4 threshold: more than 300 juveniles of mice, rats, hamsters or gerbils GIVEN AWAY per year. The statute counts animals transferred, not animals born. On transfer, the breeder must supply the species care information required by 31 Abs. 2 (31b Abs. 4). Since 19 June 2026 breeding also brings the duties of the 7. Abschnitt of the TSch-SV. The ministry confirmed in writing on 23 September 2026 (Geschaeftszahl 2026-0.792.715) that the section applies to roof rats kept for breeding, including where only a Meldung and no Bewilligung is required, because its exemption (TSch-SV 33 Abs. 1 Z 1 and 2) is limited to domesticated Haus- und Heimtiere and to cephalopods and decapods. Housing must be adequate for the species and kept clean at all times (27 Abs. 1). Records must be kept for official inspection (28 Abs. 1). Of the seven items the section lists, three (matings, births and litters, and losses) are expressly limited to dogs and cats, so for rats the list is: species, breed, sex and age of the animals actively used for mating; individual identification where possible; date and, if known, cause of death of those breeding animals; and medical treatments such as worming. The records may be handwritten or electronic and must be kept for at least five years after the litter date of the animal concerned (28 Abs. 2). They sit on top of the general TSchG 21 duty to record all medical treatments and the number of dead animals. Sick animals must be separated and treated promptly (30).
breed.governing_law: TSchG 31b Abs. 1 (breeding Meldung), Abs. 2 Z 4 (over 300 juveniles per year given away, permit under 23), Abs. 4 (care information on transfer); Tierschutz-Sonderhaltungsverordnung (BGBl. II 139/2018 idgF) 34 (no separate Meldung for wild animals already covered by the 25 Anzeige); BMASGPK ruling 2026-0.635.895. TSch-SV 1 Abs. 6a and 7. Abschnitt (27 Abs. 1 housing, 28 Abs. 1 Z 1, 2, 3 and 7 and Abs. 2 records kept five years from the litter date, 30 care), as inserted by BGBl. II 146/2026, in force 19.06.2026; TSchG 21 Abs. 1 (records of treatments and deaths) and 22a (breeder duties); BMASGPK letter 2026-0.792.715 of 23 September 2026.

sell_give.why: Private, unadvertised transfer to acquaintances is legal, but TSchG §31a prohibits ALL public advertising of animals for sale/transfer by unregistered private individuals (social media, classifieds, forums, print), regardless of the small-breeder (300 pups/yr) threshold; only registered breeders, licensed dealers, and approved shelters may advertise. So a private keeper can give a roof rat away quietly but cannot publicly advertise it without registering as a breeder (e.g. ~€27.54 in Vienna). Written husbandry info must accompany any transfer. From 1 January 2027 a breeder must also hand every new owner an easy-to-understand information leaflet covering the species' natural range and habitat, housing and social needs, diet, reproduction, any notification or permit duties (for a roof rat, the TSchG 25 Anzeige and the 31b breeding Meldung), other care points such as expected size and lifespan, and any required proof of competence (TSch-SV 29 Abs. 1). The text speaks of species offered for sale; the ministry stated in writing on 23 September 2026 that the duty applies equally when an animal is given away free of charge. Until then the statutory duty to inform on every handover still applies (TSchG 31b Abs. 4 with 31 Abs. 2).
sell_give.governing_law: TSchG §31a (Weitergabe), §31b, §31; 2. THVO §8. TSch-SV 29 Abs. 1 (information leaflet on every handover, in force 1 January 2027, BGBl. II 146/2026); TSchG 31b Abs. 4; BMASGPK letter 2026-0.792.715 of 23 September 2026 (applies to free giveaway).

transport.why: Intra-EU non-commercial transport (owner-accompanied, no sale) of pet rodents needs no veterinary health certificate (EU Reg. 2016/429 + Del. Reg. 2020/688; rodents are certificate-exempt when owner-accompanied and not for sale). Commercial intra-EU movement needs health documentation but no pre-import permit for EU-origin rodents. No Austrian import ban on R. rattus (not on the EU Union list). Note: the §8 2. THVO notification attaches on keeping, not at the border. Never release.
transport.governing_law: EU Reg. 2016/429 Arts. 245–247; Del. Reg. (EU) 2020/688; BAVG import rules; EU Reg. 1143/2014 (R. rattus not listed).

restrictions.summary: File ONE notification (Anzeige) with your district authority, the Bezirksverwaltungsbehoerde or Veterinaeramt, within two weeks of bringing the animal home, and declare breeding in that same form. The ministry confirmed on 3 August 2026 that R. rattus is a Wildtier, so TSchG 25 applies; TSch-SV 34 then means the breeding report under 31b Abs. 1 does not have to be filed separately. This is a form, not a permit, but skipping it is a breach. Notify the authority again within 14 days if you stop keeping. Never release.
steps: File the TSchG 25 Anzeige with the Bezirksverwaltungsbehoerde within two weeks of starting to keep
Declare breeding in that same Anzeige, so TSch-SV 34 removes the separate 31b Abs. 1 Meldung
Meet the rat housing standard at point 3.8 of Anlage 1 of the 2. THVO
Notify the authority within 14 days if you stop keeping (TSchG 25 Abs. 1)
Only if you give away more than 300 juveniles a year: apply for a Bewilligung under TSchG 23
Keep the TSch-SV 28 breeding records from the first litter, and hold each for five years after the litter date (see the next box)

restrictions.summary: Keep breeding records and keep them for five years. The 7. Abschnitt of the Tierschutz-Sonderhaltungsverordnung has applied to roof-rat breeders since 19 June 2026, at hobby scale too; the ministry confirmed this in writing on 23 September 2026. The records are for inspection by the authority at any time and may be on paper or electronic.
steps: Record the species, breed, sex and age of each animal actively used for mating (TSch-SV 28 Abs. 1 Z 1)
Record an individual identification for each such animal, where one is possible (28 Abs. 1 Z 2)
Record the date and, if known, the cause of death of those breeding animals (28 Abs. 1 Z 3)
Record every medical treatment, such as worming (28 Abs. 1 Z 7, and TSchG 21 Abs. 1, which also asks for the number of dead animals)
Keep each record for at least five years after the litter date of the animal concerned (28 Abs. 2)
Keep housing adequate for the species and clean at all times (27 Abs. 1); separate and treat sick animals promptly (30)
restrictions.where_to_file: Nothing to file: the records stay with the breeder for inspection by the Bezirksverwaltungsbehörde

restrictions.summary: TSchG §31a bans ALL public advertising of animals by unregistered private individuals (social media, classifieds, forums, print), regardless of the 300-pup/yr hobby threshold. Quiet private transfer to acquaintances is legal; to advertise publicly you must register as a breeder with the local veterinary authority (e.g. ~€27.54 at MA 60 Vienna), and written husbandry info must accompany any transfer. From 1 January 2027 that information must take the form of a written leaflet (TSch-SV 29), and the ministry says it is owed on a free giveaway as well as a sale.
steps: Give away quietly to acquaintances: no extra step beyond the keep/Meldung
To advertise publicly: register as a breeder with the Bezirksverwaltungsbehörde / Veterinäramt
Provide written species-specific care info to every new owner
From 1 January 2027: hand over the TSch-SV 29 information leaflet with every animal, sold or given free

inquiry_focus: (1) Does captive-bred Rattus rattus (Hausratte/Schwarzratte) kept as a privately-bred pet qualify as a 'wildes Säugetier' under §8 of the 2. Tierhaltungsverordnung, triggering the Meldepflicht to the Bezirksveterinäramt, or is it treated as a common pet rodent equivalent to R. norvegicus and exempt? (2) Is R. rattus covered by the §31b Abs. 4 TSchG small-rodent hobby-breeding carve-out (which names 'Ratten' without a species qualifier), or does its wild-species status impose the §31b Abs. 1 framework regardless of scale? (3) For intra-Austrian transfer of captive-bred R. rattus between private keepers, does the §8 notification obligation transfer to the new keeper, and is any animal-health certificate required?
